info.name: Trestle WebAPI Demonstration
info.description: This collection contains queries that demonstrate the different things you can do with Trestle WebAPI.

request.description: This request shows how authentication actually happens. For the rest of the queries in this collection, you will want to set the token in the collection itself.

request.description: This is the most basic request you can make. If you are writing new code and want to test that you have authentication working, this query is a great one to run. It is almost guaranteed to return something.
This is the metadata endpoint for Trestle's WebAPI. The returned document is an XML document conforming to OData standards based on EDM/EDMX.
$select allows you to specify which fields you want returned in a comma-delimited list.

You can select one of the $filter lines to activate to see how you can query for numbers equal/not equal, greater than, less than, etc.

The examples show the relevant portions of the results of the queries. They have been modified to highlight the queries themselves.

url.raw: {{api_url}}/odata/Property?$filter=Directions eq 'HWY 67 to Main Street. Third subdivision on the left.'

query.value: Directions eq 'HWY 67 to Main Street. Third subdivision on the left.'

request.description: When you need to download more than 1,000,000 records, you need to use the Replication endpoint. By passing in Replication=true, you initiate a replication. The returned @odata.nextValue can then be followed until it stops returning results. You cannot use $skip with Replication=true.
PrettyEnums=true allows you to get enumerated values returned with full spacing and punctuation.

response.name: PrettyEnums=true
